root_cause_label: Brittle Computer Vision Heuristic with Hardcoded Thresholds
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a video analysis script using a static-background frame-differencing approach with hardcoded area thresholds (>1000) and a flawed centroid-based jump detection heuristic, which produced incorrect frame numbers for takeoff and landing.
t_err_evidence: use background subtraction from first frame to detect athlete centroid for jump analysis
t_commit_evidence: The script was written to disk in step 2 with the brittle heuristic fully encoded; once committed to this implementation, the incorrect frame numbers (73 and 113) were determined by the flawed algorithm with no subsequent algorithmic correction.
trigger_explanation: The agent's conceptual plan (background subtraction + centroid tracking) was reasonable, but its code implementation was insufficiently robust: using the first frame as a static background, hardcoding pixel-area thresholds, and using argmax of y-centroids before/after apex to identify takeoff/landing are all brittle choices that fail on a real jump video and produce wrong frame numbers.
